headline: Computational models couple vascular structure and tissue response across organs
label: Vascular Spatial Dynamical Models
summary: Recent preprints extend mechanistic vascular models to pulmonary hemodynamics, post-lumpectomy healing, and blood-brain barrier dynamics.
synthesis: Three preprints apply mechanistic computational frameworks to vascular compartments at different scales. A multiscale hemodynamic model of the pulmonary circulation links arterial and venous trees to capillary sheets and reports that capillaries damp pulsatility in both healthy and pulmonary hypertension cases. A mechanistic model of post-lumpectomy breast healing adds inflammation and angiogenesis, with Bayesian calibration to porcine data. An agent-based model of the neurovascular unit, BBBABM, simulates blood-brain barrier injury, activation and restoration, with dose-dependent behavior. The common thread is explicit coupling of vascular structure to tissue-level dynamics, combined with calibration or representation of injury and remodeling. What is new is the extension of such frameworks beyond flow to remodeling and barrier dynamics.
